objective: Construct full homomorphisms for the two-vertex-bipartization subclass, prove its exact two-terminal attainable relation, and audit the C5 strengthening.

atomic_claims.text: Every finite simple triangle-free graph made bipartite by deleting at most two vertices has a B-homomorphism, without a degree bound.
The one-apex subclass has an explicit C5 map obtained by two commuting legal subset translations from the specified bipartite base map.
At a bipartizing nonedge pair, type 2 always occurs, type 1 occurs iff there is no common neighbor, and type 0 occurs iff there is no simple length-three path.
An eight-vertex triangle-free cubic graph with a bipartizing pair maps to B but not to C5.
Any root counterexample must require at least three vertex deletions to become bipartite.

assumptions: Finite simple triangle-free graph; a deletion set of at most two vertices and a bipartition of the remainder are available.
Vertex deletion is distinguished from edge odd-cycle transversals.
Use the fixed B and C06 generator facts; construct a new map rather than preserve an arbitrary supplied exterior map.
risks: Paper proof only; no graph enumeration, SAT or kernel execution.
The degree-free two-apex theorem is a subclass result, not the universal root.
The two-switch statement is restricted to the explicitly chosen base map.
The C5 obstruction is not a B obstruction; all old packets remain unchanged.
